node.title: Component-profile rigidity at the strict endpoint
node.statement: Factor a hypothetical first strict A=3 endpoint counterexample into irreducible bidegree components (r_i,e_i). Component root incidence gives T r_i-I_i>=T r_i-N e_i, while the aggregate row shortfall is at most O<=m-1. Hence r_i<=4e_i. Since sum_i(4e_i-r_i)=4m-(4m-1)=1, there is exactly one component with r=4e-1 and every other component has r=4e. The balanced components consume at least four shortfall units per parameter degree, so their total parameter degree is at most floor((m-1)/4); the unique defect-one component has e>=ceil((3m+1)/4). In particular Q cannot split into rational parameter branches, but the dominant nonlinear component remains open.
